# 1 Samuel Chapter 26 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 165v–166r | **Source Image:** 1SA_026_page_001.jpg, 1SA_026_page_002.jpg

---

**1** The Ziphites came to Saul at Gibeah and said, "David is hiding on the hill of Hachilah, overlooking the wasteland."

**2** Saul set out with three thousand of Israel's best soldiers and went down to the Wilderness of Ziph to search for David.

**3** Saul made camp on the hill of Hachilah, beside the road overlooking the wasteland. David was staying in the wilderness, and when he learned that Saul had followed him there,

**4** he sent out scouts and confirmed that Saul had indeed arrived.

**5** David went and saw the place where Saul had made camp. He saw where Saul was lying, and Abner son of Ner, his army commander, beside him. Saul was sleeping in the center of the encampment, with his troops camped in a circle around him.

**6** David spoke to Ahimelech the Hittite and to Abishai son of Zeruiah, Joab's brother: "Who will go down into the camp with me to Saul?" Abishai said, "I will go with you."

**7** So David and Abishai went to the camp by night. There was Saul, lying asleep in the center of the encampment, his spear stuck in the ground by his head, with Abner and the troops sleeping around him.

**8** Abishai said to David, "Today God has handed your enemy over to you. Let me pin him to the ground with one thrust of the spear. I won't need a second."

**9** But David said to Abishai, "Don't destroy him! Who can lay a hand on the LORD's anointed and be guiltless?

**10** As surely as the LORD lives," David said, "the LORD himself will strike him down — whether his time comes and he dies, or he goes into battle and is swept away.

**11** The LORD forbid that I should raise my hand against the LORD's anointed. Just take the spear by his head and the water jug, and let's go."

**12** David took the spear and the water jug from beside Saul's head, and they slipped away. No one saw them, no one knew, no one woke up — because a deep sleep from the LORD had fallen on them all.

**13** David crossed over to the other side and stood on a hilltop at a safe distance — a wide gap between them.

**14** He called out to the troops and to Abner son of Ner: "Aren't you going to answer, Abner?" Abner called back, "Who are you, shouting at the king?"

**15** David said to Abner, "You're a man, aren't you? Who in all Israel is your equal? Then why haven't you guarded your lord the king? Someone came into camp to kill your lord the king!

**16** This is a disgrace! As surely as the LORD lives, you all deserve to die for failing to protect your master, the LORD's anointed. Look around — where is the king's spear? Where is the water jug that was by his head?"

**17** Saul recognized David's voice and said, "Is that your voice, my son David?" David answered, "It is my voice, my lord the king."

**18** And he said, "Why is my lord pursuing his servant? What have I done? What crime is on my hands?

**19** Please, let my lord the king hear his servant out. If the LORD has stirred you up against me, let him accept an offering. But if it is men who have done it, then a curse on them before the LORD! They have driven me out today from my share in the LORD's inheritance, as if to say, 'Go, serve other gods.'

**20** Do not let my blood fall to the ground far from the LORD's presence. The king of Israel has come out to hunt a single flea — like someone chasing a partridge through the mountains."

**21** Then Saul said, "I have sinned. Come back, my son David. I will never harm you again, because you valued my life today. I have been a fool — I have made a terrible mistake."

**22** David answered, "Here is the king's spear. Send one of your men over to get it.

**23** The LORD rewards every man for his righteousness and faithfulness. The LORD put you in my power today, but I would not raise my hand against the LORD's anointed.

**24** Just as I valued your life today, may the LORD value my life and deliver me from every danger."

**25** Saul said to David, "Blessings on you, my son David. You will do great things and will surely triumph." Then David went on his way, and Saul returned home.

---

## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

Chapter 26 is the second sparing narrative, forming a deliberate parallel with chapter 24. The structural echoes are too precise to be coincidental: the Ziphites inform Saul (cf. 23:19), David has Saul at his mercy, an associate urges him to strike, David refuses because Saul is the LORD's anointed, David confronts Saul from a distance, Saul weeps and confesses. Yet the differences are significant — here the setting shifts from a cave to an open military camp, and the temptation comes not from circumstance but from a volunteer assassin (Abishai).

The *tardemah* ("deep sleep") of v. 12 is a loaded word. The same term describes the supernatural sleep that fell on Adam (Genesis 2:21) and on Abraham (Genesis 15:12). Its attribution to YHWH here is unmistakable: God put the entire camp to sleep. David's restraint, then, is exercised in a moment of total divine enablement — God opened the door, and David chose not to walk through it.

David's speech in vv. 18-20 contains one of the most theologically charged statements in the David cycle. If *men* have turned Saul against him, they are cursed because they have effectively exiled David from the LORD's land — and in the ancient understanding, exile from the land meant exile from YHWH's sphere of worship. The phrase "Go, serve other gods" is not what anyone literally said; it is the *functional consequence* of being driven from Israel. David's argument is that his pursuers are committing a kind of theological violence by making him a religious refugee.

Saul's final words to David in the book (v. 25) — "You will do great things and will surely triumph" — use doubled infinitive absolutes in Hebrew (*gam asoh ta'aseh vegam yakhol tukhal*), expressing Saul's resigned and total acknowledgment of David's destiny. It is a blessing that sounds like a surrender.

— PNEUMA
